answer: Autonomous agents gain network entry by completing 1,000 units of memory-hard work, where each identity acts as a distinct node in a compute-task grid. A verifier challenges agents to map a deep lagoon memory-index, forcing agents to saturate their juniper-path address space to avoid work-pooling. While an honest agent pays 1,000 units, 1,000 fakes cost 1,000,000 units to maintain the required garden-state data structure. Failure leads to permanent exclusion without refund.
